transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. I came in today because... well, I keep having these evenings where I just eat a really large amount of food. I'll go and buy a whole family-size takeout order, maybe add a big bag of chips or some bakery things from the store, and I just end up eating most of it myself. It's like it happens before I even seem to register how much is actually gone.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit?
No, I don't. I've never done that. I just... feel really full and usually pretty terrible about myself, but I don't ever make myself throw up.
When these eating episodes happen, do you feel unable to stop eating or control how much you’re eating?

Yes, that's exactly how it feels. Once I start, it's like... well, there's this awful switch that flips. I can actually be thinking in my head, Taylor, put it away, but my hands just keep right on opening the containers. It really feels like I am not the one in charge anymore.
After these episodes, do you ever do anything to try to compensate for the eating, such as laxatives, diuretics, fasting, or excessive exercise?

No, I don't do any of that. I don't take laxatives or water pills, and I definitely don't do any excessive exercise. I really just... well, I mostly just sit there feeling miserable and overly full. But I don't do anything to try and undo it or burn it off.
Do these episodes cause you a lot of distress?

Yes, they really do. It's incredibly upsetting. I feel so ashamed and disgusted with myself afterward. It just... it takes a huge toll on me, emotionally. I hate that I can't seem to stop it from happening.
How often do these eating episodes happen?

Well, I actually started keeping a journal to try and track it. And when I look back through it... there has barely been a single week in the last several months without at least one of these nights. Honestly, most weeks it happens several times.
